runtime.description: Raw credential value; prefixes and API-key locations are supplied from the contract scheme.
runtime.scope: Core OpenAPI CLI contract-test credential generation in OSS 2.55.3 and Enterprise 1.28.3, with the separate core mock boundary demonstrated. Other integrations and authored example/dictionary interactions need independent review.

Dictionary/generated request values can follow when no configured/environment credential exists. Example-level credentials have additional consumers; this is not universal request precedence. An empty scheme-named environment value is present and suppresses the JVM/global fallback; this differs from a blank config token being skipped.
runtime.caveat: The V3 map lookup selects systemUnderTest and matching spec ID, then exact scheme name. Schema-accepted dependency maps do not establish mock token authentication. runtime.effect: Applies test or mock behavior settings to this tested service; reusable component settings acquire their role at the use site.

keys.title: JUnit report directory
keys.description: Directory where JUnit reports are written.

schema.title: JUnit report directory
schema.description: Directory where JUnit reports are written.

runtime.scope: JUnit XML reports from the core CLI test command. Other report formats and direct JUnit launchers have separate output configuration.
runtime.effect: Chooses the directory for the core CLI JUnit XML report. Use it when CI needs a predictable location for the test-results artifact.
runtime.omission: The V3 accessor returns no configured report directory. Without the CLI flag either, the core command does not request this XML report; governance/report settings are separate.
runtime.precedence: The core CLI --junitReportDir value wins over the service setting, which wins over the global specmatic.settings.test setting. This accessor has no environment/property fallback.
runtime.caveat: The ordinary core CLI uses a relative report directory from the process working directory, including when the value comes from a nested config file. Path-rebasing tools can transform this field through mapPaths; ordinary config loading does not perform that rebasing. Keep the output directory writable. This key does not select HTML, CTRF or every report type.
runtime.example: junitReportDir: ./build/test-results writes TEST-junit-jupiter.xml under that configured directory when running through the core CLI.

assertions: A report directory inherited from global settings produces reports/TEST-junit-jupiter.xml with a testcase for handbook.
A nested config with an absolute contract directory writes relative report output from the process root, not the config directory.

keys.title: Lenient mode
keys.description: Allow lenient validation behavior during tests.

schema.title: Lenient mode
schema.description: Allow lenient validation behavior during tests.

runtime.scope: Core OpenAPI parsing and example loading. CLI and JUnit entry points differ; do not transfer this setting to other protocol parsers.
runtime.effect: Allows selected parser/collector failures to be reported while loading continues. It does not make every invalid contract usable or disable response checks during test execution.
runtime.omission: The accessor falls back to SPECMATIC_TEST_LENIENT_MODE from the environment, then the JVM property. Core parsing uses false for an absent value. One external-example failure gate specifically checks for explicit false, so an unresolved null is not identical to false in every path.
runtime.precedence: A non-null tested-service value overrides the global specmatic.settings.test value field by field. Missing fields continue to inherit; explicit false is a value, not an instruction to fall back. Without staged modes, config wins over SPECMATIC_TEST_LENIENT_MODE. The core CLI stages false when --lenient is omitted, overriding a true config value; use --lenient to enable it for that core CLI run. A JUnit invocation without a staged mode can use the config value.
runtime.caveat: Leniency only applies to specific recovery paths. Partial failures may already be logged and returned regardless of this flag, and later example validation can still fail. Keep the original error visible and fix the contract where possible.
runtime.example: For core CLI parsing leniency, use --lenient even if the file contains lenientMode: true. A direct JUnit configuration without a mode override reads the configured value.

keys.title: Maximum test count
keys.description: Maximum number of tests to execute.

schema.title: Maximum test count
schema.description: Maximum number of tests to execute.

runtime.scope: Core JUnit contract-test execution. This note does not assert a suite-wide limit for separate Enterprise protocol runners.
runtime.effect: Runs at most the selected number of otherwise executable scenarios. Subsequent executable scenarios are marked skipped with MAX_TEST_COUNT_EXCEEDED. Scenarios already classified as non-executable do not consume this count.
runtime.omission: A missing configuration value falls back to MAX_TEST_COUNT from the environment, then the JVM property. If all are absent, the JUnit runner leaves the scenario sequence uncapped.
runtime.precedence: A non-null tested-service value wins over the global specmatic.settings.test value, then MAX_TEST_COUNT from the environment, then the JVM property. Other test settings continue to inherit independently.
runtime.caveat: At this runner's execution-selection step, 0 or a negative value skips every executable scenario; it does not mean unlimited. Use omission for no cap, and a positive integer for a useful cap. Invalid numeric environment/property text fails conversion.
runtime.example: With maxTestCount: 1, the first executable scenario runs and later executable scenarios are skipped. Increasing maxTestRequestCombinations does not override this execution limit.

assertions: Without a cap, two authored examples execute successfully.
Service maxTestCount: 1 executes one successful example instead of two.

keys.title: Maximum request combinations
keys.description: Maximum request combinations generated for a test.

schema.title: Maximum request combinations
schema.description: Maximum request combinations generated for a test.

runtime.scope: Core schema-based request generation used by HTTP contract testing. Protocol DTOs and other runners need their own applicability review.
runtime.effect: Caps the candidate combinations produced by the core request-pattern combination generator. Use it to bound the expansion of requests with multiple candidate values. This is not a cap on the total number of contract tests.
runtime.omission: The configuration accessor falls back to MAX_TEST_REQUEST_COMBINATIONS, first from the environment then the JVM property. If all are absent, core generation uses Int.MAX_VALUE (2,147,483,647), effectively no smaller configured cap.
runtime.precedence: A non-null service value wins over the global specmatic.settings.test value; the selected config value wins over MAX_TEST_REQUEST_COMBINATIONS from the environment and JVM property. Settings merge field by field, so overriding this field does not discard other global test settings.
runtime.caveat: Choose a positive integer. The resolved schema's integer type alone does not establish a usable limit: CombinationSpec rejects values below 1 when generation reaches it. Invalid numeric environment/property text throws during numeric conversion; it is not silently replaced with the default.
runtime.example: Use 20 to limit combination expansion for requests with many candidate values. Several operations or examples can still produce more than 20 tests overall; use maxTestCount for an execution cap.

keys.title: Test parallelism
keys.description: Parallel execution setting for generated tests.

schema.title: Test parallelism
schema.description: Parallel execution setting for generated tests.

runtime.scope: Core CLI scheduling of JUnit contract tests. Merely reading a config in a custom JUnit integration does not apply the CLI scheduler setup.
runtime.effect: Selects automatic or fixed JUnit parallel execution in the core CLI. Use auto for the dynamic strategy, or a quoted positive integer for a fixed worker count.
runtime.omission: Falls back to SPECMATIC_TEST_PARALLELISM from the environment, then the JVM property. With no value, the core CLI leaves JUnit parallel-execution properties unchanged; external JUnit configuration may still affect scheduling.
runtime.precedence: Service configuration overrides global configuration, then the environment and JVM fallback. The selected value is applied to JUnit execution properties by the core CLI before execution.
runtime.caveat: This is a string field: use "4", not an unquoted YAML integer. The CLI accepts auto or parses an integer; positive values are needed for useful fixed parallelism. Do not use an empty string, zero or a negative value to request serial execution. It controls test execution, not source fetching or all protocol workers.
runtime.example: parallelism: "4" enables the fixed strategy with four workers. Omit the key and its fallback inputs when you want the CLI to leave JUnit scheduling configuration alone.

keys.title: Schema resiliency tests
keys.description: Select all, positive-only, or no schema resiliency tests.

schema.title: Schema resiliency tests
schema.description: Select all, positive-only, or no schema resiliency tests.

runtime.scope: Core schema-based positive/negative contract-test generation. MockSettings has a separate similarly named key; this note covers TestSettings.
runtime.effect: Selects all positive and negative schema-derived tests, positiveOnly, or none. Use it to expand beyond authored example tests. none turns off this generation mode; authored tests can still run.
runtime.omission: The accessor derives a suite from SPECMATIC_GENERATIVE_TESTS and ONLY_POSITIVE, each read from the environment before the JVM property. SPECMATIC_GENERATIVE_TESTS=true selects all; otherwise ONLY_POSITIVE=true selects positiveOnly; otherwise the suite is none.
runtime.precedence: An explicit staged JUnit generative mode can enable/disable resiliency ahead of config. Otherwise a non-null service value overrides the global test value, then flag-derived selection. An explicit none suppresses those flag fallbacks.
runtime.caveat: resiliencyTests is an accepted alias under this V3 TestSettings object. Prefer schemaResiliencyTests and supply only one spelling. More generated requests can require a dictionary, matching authentication and application handling of invalid inputs; selecting all is not proof those prerequisites are met.
runtime.example: schemaResiliencyTests: positiveOnly generates positive schema variations. Switch to all when you also want invalid-input scenarios; choose none for authored example tests without that expansion.

keys.title: Strict mode
keys.description: Enable strict validation behavior during tests.

schema.title: Strict mode
schema.description: Enable strict validation behavior during tests.

runtime.scope: Core OpenAPI contract loading, dictionary selection and test generation. Separate protocol runners require their own review.
runtime.effect: Requires usable example data in strict-sensitive paths. For example, a named response example without a matching request example fails when the operation can have a named request example; dictionary values present at a JSON path must match its schema.
runtime.omission: The accessor falls back to SPECMATIC_TEST_STRICT_MODE from the environment, then the JVM property. Core contract loading uses false if none supplies a value.
runtime.precedence: A non-null tested-service value overrides the global specmatic.settings.test value field by field. Missing fields continue to inherit; explicit false is a value, not an instruction to fall back. An explicitly supplied core CLI --strict or staged JUnit mode is applied to the service ahead of config. Otherwise config wins over the environment/property fallback.
runtime.caveat: Strictness is not a universal response-validation toggle. It is used by several example, substitution and dictionary paths. strictMode and lenientMode are independent settings; neither silently negates the other.
runtime.example: If the contract has a named response example but lacks the corresponding request example for a parameterized operation, strictMode: true can fail loading rather than generating missing request data. Supply the matching request example to correct the contract.

keys.title: Test timeout
keys.description: Maximum request duration in milliseconds.

schema.title: Test timeout
schema.description: Maximum request duration in milliseconds.

runtime.scope: Core HTTP contract testing through the CLI/JUnit runner in OSS 2.55.3 and Enterprise 1.28.3. Other protocol-specific timeout fields have separate behavior.
runtime.effect: Sets the HTTP test request timeout in milliseconds. Use it when a correct API response takes longer than the normal request timeout; it does not set a timeout for the whole test suite.
runtime.omission: When neither configuration nor SPECMATIC_TEST_TIMEOUT supplies a value, the core JUnit contract-test runner uses 6,000 milliseconds. This is a runner default, not a default inserted into the YAML.
runtime.precedence: An explicit core CLI --timeout-in-ms wins over --timeout (seconds). That CLI value is applied to the tested service. Otherwise a non-null service setting wins over the global specmatic.settings.test value, then SPECMATIC_TEST_TIMEOUT from the environment, then the JVM property of the same name, then the runner default.
runtime.caveat: Omission and explicit null fall back during model merging; the resolved schema rejects null for this integer field. A quoted number or empty string is not an integer. Do not use 0 as a portable way to disable timeouts: transport behavior is separate from this setting's fallback rules.
runtime.example: Set the global value to 10000 and a service value to 2500: that service uses 2500 ms. A core CLI --timeout-in-ms 8000 then selects 8000 ms for that run.

assertions: Service 1000 ms overrides global 20 ms and two delayed requests pass.
Service 20 ms overrides global 1000 ms and exits 1 with a request timeout.
CLI --timeout-in-ms 4000 overrides service 20 ms and two delayed requests pass.

keys.title: Source URL
keys.description: Remote specification source URL.

schema.title: Source URL
schema.description: Remote specification source URL.

runtime.scope: V3 source selection and the traced core CLI consumers. The linked executed recipes cover OpenAPI mocks in OSS 2.55.3 and Enterprise 1.28.3; separate protocol/integration behavior and private transports require their own verification.
runtime.effect: Sets the HTTP(S) specification-download base. The checked resolver joins the base and each relative spec path with a slash; it does not set an API target.
runtime.omission: Required for a selected web source. Omission or a blank value is invalid; no environment fallback is implicit in this field. Use an authored template if variation is needed.
runtime.precedence: The base keeps its path even when a spec starts with a slash. One trailing slash on the base and one leading slash on the spec are removed by the join. Absolute spec URIs are rejected.
runtime.caveat: The loader writes under the config directory’s .specmatic/web and downloads during loading. The local-path calculation uses host/base path/spec path, omitting port/query; it is not a unique origin key or immutable/offline cache guarantee. These examples do not verify authenticated hosts, redirects or every query/fragment form.
runtime.example: Base http://127.0.0.1:9200/contracts and spec books.yaml fetch /contracts/books.yaml. The checked /books.yaml spec still fetches that same base path.

assertions: Normal base, trailing-base slash and leading-spec slash request the same path and cache the exact supplied bytes.
Absolute spec URI and empty web URL fail config validation with code 1.

schema.title: Web source options
schema.description: Remote URL settings for this web source.

runtime.scope: V3 source selection and the traced core CLI consumers. The linked executed recipes cover OpenAPI mocks in OSS 2.55.3 and Enterprise 1.28.3; separate protocol/integration behavior and private transports require their own verification.
runtime.effect: Chooses downloading specs from a web base URL. The selected specs are appended to its url, and the downloaded files feed the operation.
runtime.omission: Web is optional only as a provider choice. When selected, its url must be present and nonblank; there is no default specification host.
runtime.precedence: Mutually exclusive with filesystem and git. This source URL is independent of the tested API URL or mock listener.
runtime.caveat: The V3 web provider uses ResolvedWebSource, not the legacy direct-URL downloader. Its append and cache-path rules must not be inferred from generic URI resolution.
runtime.example: Use web: {url: http://127.0.0.1:9200/contracts} with specs: [books.yaml] to load the demonstrated spec.

assertions: The source receives GET /contracts/books.yaml and the mock serves the authored book on a separate port.

runtime.scope: V3 local SOAP 1.1 configuration in OSS 2.55.3 and Enterprise 1.28.3. Reusable components affect a run only when selected by a service.
runtime.effect: Sets the complete mock listener origin.
runtime.omission: When absent, host/port supplies an origin only if port is present; otherwise this model supplies no origin.
runtime.precedence: A matching per-spec origin wins over this service origin. Within this object, non-null baseUrl wins over host and port.
runtime.caveat: In OSS 2.55.3 and Enterprise 1.28.3, relative local WSDL paths can miss the mock endpoint lookup and use the CLI listener instead. keys.title: Mock certificate
keys.description: TLS certificate settings or a reference to a named certificate.

schema.title: Mock certificate
schema.description: TLS certificate settings or a reference to a named certificate.

runtime.scope: V3 local SOAP 1.1 configuration in OSS 2.55.3 and Enterprise 1.28.3. Reusable components affect a run only when selected by a service.
runtime.effect: Supplies inline or referenced HTTPS key-store/mTLS configuration for the selected WSDL service.
runtime.omission: No cert means no WSDL-specific certificate registry entry. The host/port model uses http without cert and https when cert is present.

schema.description: Host on which the mock service listens.

runtime.effect: Sets the hostname or bind address used with port.
runtime.omission: The model uses 0.0.0.0 when port is supplied and host is omitted. Host alone supplies no origin if both baseUrl and port are absent.
